headline: Beartooth Highway Seasonal Opening and Pass Requirements
reservation: There is no toll or reservation required for the highway itself, but the route passes through National Forest lands and enters Yellowstone National Park. Yellowstone requires a separate entry fee or pass at the Northeast Entrance; check the official NPS site for changing entry requirements and seasonal road opening dates.

days.title: High Alpine Peaks and Plateaus

stops.name: Rock Creek Vista Point
stops.detail: Climb the switchbacks to this overlook for a dramatic view back toward the Hellroaring Plateau.

stops.name: Beartooth Pass Summit
stops.detail: Stand at 10,947 feet for a 360-degree view of the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness peaks.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours for the 68-mile drive; grades are steep and weather is unpredictable.
days.note: Even in mid-summer, snow can fall at the summit, potentially closing the road temporarily.

days.title: Glacial Lakes and Granite Walls

stops.name: Beartooth Lake
stops.detail: Observe the reflection of Beartooth Butte in the alpine waters, a popular spot for photography and short walks.

stops.name: Clay Butte Lookout
stops.detail: Follow the spur road to a historic fire tower for views extending into the Clarks Fork Valley.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for exploring spurs; gravel road conditions vary with recent rainfall.
days.note: The turnoff to Clay Butte is unpaved; check vehicle clearance before proceeding.

days.title: Yellowstone Gateway Descent

stops.name: Pilot and Index Peaks Viewpoint
stops.detail: Capture the iconic silhouettes of these sharp volcanic spires near the Wyoming border.

stops.name: Chief Joseph Scenic Byway Junction
stops.detail: Transition toward the Sunlight Basin or continue to the Yellowstone Northeast Entrance.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; heavy motorcycle and RV traffic is common during peak summer months.
days.note: Descending toward Cooke City involves sharp curves that require managed braking.

intel.title: Summit Turnouts
intel.text: Parking at the Beartooth Pass sign is limited and often crowded during midday. Use larger pullouts located slightly below the crest for safer viewing opportunities.

intel.title: Alpine Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect no cellular service between Red Lodge and Cooke City. Download offline maps and notify others of your travel plans before leaving the gateway towns.

intel.title: High Elevation Services
intel.text: There is no fuel available on the 68-mile stretch between Red Lodge and Cooke City. Top off in Red Lodge to account for the heavy fuel consumption during the steep ascent.

intel.title: Seasonal Window
intel.text: The highway typically opens late May and closes by mid-October, though storms can trigger closures anytime. Verify current status via the Montana and Wyoming Departments of Transportation.

intel.title: Vehicle Length Restrictions
intel.text: While open to RVs, the steep grades and tight hairpins near Rock Creek can be challenging for long trailers. Check for specific length advisories at the Red Lodge visitor center.

plan.arrival: Pick up rentals at Billings Logan International; drive to Red Lodge for overnight acclimation before the high-altitude climb.
plan.vehicle: Cars with good brakes are essential; large RVs should use low gears during the descent to prevent brake overheating.
plan.goldenHour: Rock Creek Vista Point offers spectacular morning light, though the sun disappears early behind the high western ridges.
